SUBTLEX-UK Explorer

Frequency data for 160,022 words from British TV subtitles. Filter the list on the left and every chart and the word table update to match.

Proper names make up about 39% of the list.

Zipf score distribution

Zipf = log10 of occurrences per million words + 3. Below 3 is low frequency, 4 and above is high. The tall bar at 1.17 holds words seen only about 3 times.

Word length

Click a bar to filter to that length. Longer words are rarer on average.

Part of speech

Each spelling carries its most common part of speech. Click a bar to show only that category.

Frequency curve

Zipf score by rank among the matching words, on a log rank axis. A few words are very common; most are rare.

Contextual diversity vs. frequency

CD is the share of programmes containing the word. Each dot is a word (a sample of up to 2,500).

Matching words

How to read this

Rank is the position in the full list when words are ordered by Zipf score, with ties broken by contextual diversity. “Top” keeps only words at or above that rank, and the other filters apply on top of it.

Data: SUBTLEX-UK (van Heuven, Mandera, Keuleers & Brysbaert, 2014), word frequencies from British television subtitles.
